environment: In-app browser, local standalone HTML served on 127.0.0.1

checks.name: Every section under all four presentation presets
checks.evidence: Source block count and order matched original view. All fixed block text matched original-view text. No mismatches.

checks.name: Comparison views
checks.evidence: All source blocks remained present. Each available comparison's original passage matched its original-view paragraph.

checks.name: Section 4.2 gaming preset
checks.evidence: Gaming analogy and challenge practice appeared. Original inventory example retained 8.0 billion, 8.4 billion, and 400 million bushels.

checks.name: Guided and challenge feedback
checks.evidence: Incorrect and correct challenge responses produced different feedback. Guided hint and correct numerical-answer feedback appeared.

checks.name: Persistence
checks.evidence: Temporary note and marked-read state survived reload, along with the selected analogy. Test note and marked-read state were then cleared through the UI.

checks.name: Desktop layout
checks.evidence: Three-column layout and controls visually inspected. An initially malformed dropdown option was repaired and verified.

checks.name: Phone layout
checks.evidence: Document width equaled viewport width. Personalize panel opened at 340 px and closed. Section dropdown navigated to 4.6; restored tables had four and five rows respectively. Viewport override reset afterward.

limits: Preservation checks compare the rendered prototype to its stored normalized capture; they do not independently verify every transcription against the live site.
Prepared narrative variants and supplemental teaching material require subject-expert semantic review.
These checks establish interface behavior and source preservation, not learning effectiveness.
Notes export, print output, external activity, and all individual custom marker combinations were not separately exercised.
